name: Insurance Comparison Platforms
description: Insurance comparison platforms bring quotations and purchasing tools from multiple insurers into a shared interface. Iranian examples illustrate how comparison, policy issuance, installment payments, and customer assistance can be combined, although their public descriptions do not establish market completeness or independently measured service quality. [s1][s2]

seo.title: Insurance Comparison Platforms in Iran | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: How Iranian insurance comparison platforms present quotations, support purchases, and differ from the insurers providing coverage.

content.heading: A shared interface for different insurers
content.content:
Insurance comparison platforms make an otherwise fragmented purchasing process easier to navigate by presenting products from different providers in one place. Azki advertises comparison of insurance prices and services alongside online purchasing and installment options. Bimeh.com likewise presents quotation, comparison, and purchase as connected services. These are descriptions of their offered functions, rather than independently verified findings about customer outcomes. [s1][s2]

The distinction between a distribution platform and an insurer matters. The International Association of Insurance Supervisors, an international standard-setting body, treats insurance intermediation as an activity involving the solicitation, negotiation, or sale of insurance. Its framework distinguishes this activity from supplementary work such as claims administration and loss appraisal. A platform can therefore participate in several stages of the customer relationship without those functions becoming interchangeable. This international framework supplies terminology; it does not establish an individual Iranian platform’s authorization. [s3]

content.heading: Why quotations require personal and vehicle information
content.content:
Bimeh.com’s motor third-party insurance interface illustrates how comparison depends on structured inputs. It offers an inquiry route using a vehicle registration plate and the plate owner’s national identification code, as well as a route without a plate. Its published explanation says that vehicle details and previous policy information feed the quotation process. This is a specific product workflow, not evidence that every insurance category uses identical questions. [s2]

The same page identifies vehicle characteristics, use, selected financial coverage, and claims-free history among the inputs relevant to price. Consequently, two displayed premiums are meaningful comparisons only when the underlying coverage and customer information are aligned. Installment availability introduces another distinction: the platform explains that participating insurers offering this option are identified within its quotation results. A payment arrangement should therefore be understood separately from the insurance protection being compared. [s2]

content.heading: What public descriptions cannot establish
content.content:
Neither inspected purchasing interface establishes that its results constitute an exhaustive, independently ranked survey of the market. This research also did not inspect platform commission agreements or ranking algorithms. Claims about the cheapest offer, impartial ordering, or superior claims service would require additional evidence.

The useful editorial distinction is between making alternatives visible and proving their relative quality. The inspected pages support an account of comparison and purchasing functions. They do not support a league table of platforms, an estimate of their market shares, or a conclusion about which insurer consistently delivers better outcomes. [s1][s2]

name: Automated Insurance Case Processing
description: Automated insurance case processing applies software to document intake, information extraction, contractual checks, and transfers between operational teams. Iranian service descriptions show both expert-led online claims workflows and advertised document-processing automation, but do not establish nationwide adoption or independently verified performance. [s1][s2]

seo.title: Automated Insurance Case Processing in Iran | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Document extraction, policy checks, expert assessment, and the evidence needed to evaluate insurance automation in Iran.

content.heading: Online submission and automated decisions are different stages
content.content:
An insurance case can move through a website while still depending on people for assessment and approval. Azki’s published motor-claim journey is an instructive example: customers identify the insurance type and parties, submit policy and accident information, and provide further details. An expert then contacts the customer for vehicle assessment. The described payment stage follows the expert’s calculation and the injured party’s approval. This documents a digitally coordinated service with explicit human involvement. [s1]

For readers encountering claims about automation, the central question is therefore which task the software performs. Collecting information, extracting it from documents, checking it against policy conditions, and authorizing a payment are distinct activities. Their separation is visible when Azki’s expert-led description is read alongside Kavan’s advertised document-processing functions. [s1][s2]

content.heading: From documents to a financial handoff
content.content:
Kavan, an Iranian insurance technology vendor, describes optical character recognition, or OCR, for reading documents and images. Its published functions include identifying services, applying contractual coverage and tariff rules, calculating claims, flagging suspicious patterns, and passing approved results to a finance unit. It also advertises operational dashboards for following case status. These are vendor descriptions of capabilities; inspected material did not establish their performance in a named insurer’s production environment. [s2]

The following diagram summarizes that advertised sequence. It should be read as a functional map of one vendor’s description, rather than a universal Iranian insurance procedure. In particular, a handoff to finance does not itself demonstrate that payment has been executed or received. [s2]

content.title: Kavan’s advertised document-processing sequence
content.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Submitted claim documents"] -->|"Document reading"| B["Extracted information"]
  B -->|"Service identification and contractual checks"| C["Claim evaluation"]
  C -->|"Flag suspicious patterns"| D["Further examination"]
  C -->|"Transfer approved results"| E["Finance unit"]
```
content.summary: The arrows describe advertised information processing and referral functions. They do not establish automatic approval, successful payment, or deployment across the Iranian insurance industry.

content.heading: Records remain part of the system
content.content:
Iran’s Electronic Commerce Act provides historical legal context for electronic records: the text hosted by WIPO recognizes electronic evidence and connects its evidential weight to security methods. Its personal-data provisions also address consent, specified purposes, and the accuracy of stored information. These provisions explain why document integrity and personal information belong in an account of insurance automation. They do not establish the current legal requirements for a particular claims engine. [s3]

A defensible assessment of automation would need deployment evidence, error measurements, and a clear account of who reviews disputed results. Those materials were not verified here. The supported conclusion is narrower: publicly described Iranian workflows combine digital intake, specialist assessment, and advertised rules-based processing in different ways. [s1][s2]

name: E-commerce
description: Iranian e-commerce encompasses broad online catalogs, seller marketplaces, specialist retailers, and channels connecting digital discovery with ordering and delivery. Public platform interfaces reveal different commercial models, while reported national transaction values require careful separation from retail sales, platform revenue, and inflation-adjusted growth. [s1][s2][s3][s4]

seo.title: E-commerce in Iran: Platforms, Purchasing and Data | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Explore Iran’s online retail models, seller marketplaces, specialist stores, and the limits of reported national e-commerce statistics.

content.heading: Several markets behind one label
content.content:
Iranian e-commerce becomes easier to understand when different kinds of online business are considered separately. Digikala’s public catalog spans electronics, household goods, clothing, and personal-care products. Basalam presents itself as a marketplace connecting buyers directly with sellers, with categories extending from food and handicrafts to furniture. Khanoumi’s catalog gives greater prominence to cosmetics, skin care, hair care, and personal care, while also listing additional categories. These interfaces document differences in merchandising and presentation; they do not independently establish market leadership or sales shares. [s1][s2][s3]

The distinction matters because a broad catalog, a seller marketplace, and a specialist retailer organize discovery differently. A broad catalog groups many kinds of purchases within one destination. A marketplace makes the seller relationship more visible. A specialist catalog can organize a product field into more detailed subcategories, as Khanoumi does for skin and hair care. These are interpretations of the inspected interfaces, rather than claims about every transaction each company handles. [s1][s2][s3]

content.heading: The transaction continues beyond product discovery
content.content:
The inspected sites also show that online commerce involves more than displaying products. Digikala describes delivery choices and product returns. Basalam presents bank-gateway payment, a refund guarantee, direct communication, and support as parts of its proposition; it also provides seller-management and developer links. These published functions connect the storefront to payment, fulfillment, and the continuing buyer–seller relationship. Their presence on a website does not establish consistent service quality or delivery coverage in every location. [s1][s2]

For an international reader, Basalam’s emphasis on direct contact is particularly useful for understanding the marketplace model. The seller remains part of the shopping experience rather than disappearing behind a single catalog identity. Its wholesale and organizational-purchasing links also indicate that consumer shopping and purchasing for businesses can coexist within a wider platform ecosystem. They do not establish the size of business-to-business trade. [s2]

content.heading: What the reported national values measure—and leave unresolved
content.content:
A Digiato article published in October 2025 attributes successive annual e-commerce transaction values to the acting head of Iran’s E-Commerce Development Center. The observations reproduced below retain the source’s Solar Hijri year labels and nominal toman denomination. They are reported national aggregates, rather than audited revenue figures for the platforms discussed here. [s4]

The sequence rises in nominal terms. That alone cannot establish an equivalent increase in the quantity of goods and services purchased: price changes also affect monetary totals. No inflation adjustment or foreign-currency conversion has been applied. More fundamentally, the underlying national report’s full methodology could not be inspected because both the official PDF and an identified mirror returned access errors. The annual values are therefore presented as a reported sequence with unresolved comparability questions, rather than as a validated retail-market trend. [s4]

Only the consecutive observations explicitly given in the inspected retrospective account are included. Earlier years and more recent full-year results have not been filled in from forecasts, mixed secondary accounts, or assumptions about release schedules. A line chart is withheld until the underlying definitions and treatment of payment channels can be checked.

content.title: Reported national e-commerce transaction values, Solar Hijri 1400–1403

content.heading: Trust depends on information and follow-through
content.content:
The Electronic Commerce Act text hosted by WIPO provides historical context for the information accompanying online purchases. Its consumer-protection provisions address supplier identity, costs, contract terms, after-sales information, and withdrawal, with qualifications and exclusions elsewhere in the text. This establishes the subjects addressed by that legislation; it does not establish current enforcement or determine the outcome of a particular dispute. [s5]

The most useful way to explore this field is therefore to connect each commercial model to its operating responsibilities: who presents the offer, who supplies the item, how payment is handled, and how delivery or returns are addressed. The platform pages make some of these functions visible. National totals answer a different question and should not substitute for evidence about individual businesses, regional access, or consumer outcomes. [s1][s2][s4]
